title: Physics II for the life sciences
purpose: Apply electric charge, fields, potential and capacitance, circuits, bioelectricity, magnetism and induction, electromagnetic waves, geometric and wave optics, the eye, atomic and nuclear physics, medical imaging and radiation safety.

blocks.deliverable: Model a cell membrane as a capacitor.
Explain conduction along a nerve with a circuit model.
Explain the magnetic fields used in MRI.
Week 7 midterm; trace rays through a lens and find the image.
Compute the lens power that corrects myopia.
Compare doses from common imaging studies.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Imaging physics brief: explain how X-ray, CT, MRI and ultrasound form images, and compare their radiation doses and their main risks and benefits.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
